examples.title: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 earnings story
examples.description: An AI-drafted earnings story. Most figures are right, but one growth rate compares the wrong quarters and one EPS figure is on the wrong accounting basis.
examples.text:
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) delivered another blowout quarter. Revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 reached a record $96.2 billion, up 18% from a year ago, as hyperscalers kept pouring money into AI infrastructure and the Vera Rubin platform began shipping in volume.

Data Center revenue was $89.0 billion, accounting for more than nine-tenths of total sales. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75.0%, roughly in line with the prior quarter despite the cost of ramping a new architecture.

Profits kept pace with sales. Operating income climbed to $63.7 billion, and GAAP net income reached $59.7 billion. GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.22.

Operating expenses rose to $8.4 billion as the company stepped up spending on networking, software and the next generation of systems.

Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects third-quarter revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, which would set yet another record and suggests demand is still running ahead of supply.

examples.title: Meta Q3 2026 earnings story
examples.description: AI-written coverage of Meta's third quarter with three planted slips, including millions written for billions.
examples.text:
Meta Platforms posted third-quarter 2026 revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year over year, as stronger ad pricing and more impressions lifted its family of apps. The quarter also showed how quickly the company's AI build-out is eating into its margins.

The bill for that ambition keeps rising. Total costs and expenses jumped to $42.0 billion, driven by depreciation on new data centers and hiring for its superintelligence lab. Research and development alone came to $20.1 billion. As a result, operating income fell to $12.99 million, well below the level of a year earlier.

Net income was $9.86 billion, or $3.38 per diluted share. Cash flow from operations held up at $32.8 billion, giving Meta room to keep funding new capacity even as investors ask when the spending will pay off.

examples.title: June-quarter roundup, as of July 29
examples.description: Microsoft, Alphabet and JPMorgan in one roundup, checked as of noon ET on July 29, before Microsoft reported. One figure belongs to the wrong company, and time travel flags what wasn't public yet.
examples.text:
Big Tech and big banks: the June-quarter scorecard

JPMorgan Chase kicked off the season on July 14 with second-quarter net income of $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per diluted share. Net revenue rose to $57.3 billion as trading and investment banking fees surged.

Alphabet followed on July 22. Revenue climbed 24% from a year earlier to $119.8 billion, and operating income reached $40.8 billion as Google Cloud kept gaining share. Alphabet earned $7.70 per diluted share.

Microsoft capped the stretch with fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $90.0 billion and diluted earnings of $4.81 per share, as Azure demand continued to outstrip the capacity the company can bring online.

Taken together, the three reports suggest that spending on AI is still accelerating heading into the second half, and that the banks financing it are doing just fine.
examples.context: Microsoft, Alphabet and JPMorgan Chase, quarter ended June 30, 2026
